eli5.text: The AI coding assistant now refuses to apply a file edit that appears to have been cut off mid-generation instead of writing a broken, half-finished version of your file to disk. This matters when a response hits the output token limit or the connection drops while the assistant is writing a large file, which previously left your file with an incomplete fragment like code ending in `ui.horizontal_wrapped(ui` instead of a complete program. The change protects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who rely on the assistant editing their files, so you will now get a clear error telling you nothing was written and suggesting smaller, targeted edits via str_replace rather than silently corrupting your file with a truncated copy.

ai.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff CLI manifest to 0.1.11. A new `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` was added to the Axiom-only log allowlist to track these refusals. eli5.text: This release introduces a protective check that stops the AI assistant from accidentally overwriting your files with incomplete code. Previously, if an AI response hit its length limit while trying to save a large file, it could leave the code on your computer in a broken, half-finished state. Now, the assistant recognizes when a file change is cut off or unusually short and refuses to apply it, keeping your original code exactly as it was. It also improves how it explains these situations to itself, telling it to make smaller, more careful changes instead of trying to send the same large command that failed. Finally, the release includes internal logging updates that let the service operators see exactly when these protective blocks happen, without storing the actual contents of your files.

These fields are supported by two new type definitions, `FreebuffCountryVerificationReason` and `FreebuffPlanUpsell`, which model when country verification is ineffective and what paid plan to offer in that case. The `countryUpsell` block is built server-side from the plan catalog so all clients render identical figures for limited-access accounts.

eli5.text: The system now sends free-tier users in restricted regions specific information about whether verifying their location can actually change their access level. If it cannot, the message includes a detailed offer showing exactly how many daily credit units they would receive if they upgraded to a paid plan. This change prepares the interface to display accurate upgrade offers for people whose region currently limits their free usage, but no visible updates appear until the user-facing apps are updated to read and display this new data.

ai.title: Freebuff auth token moves to OS keychain via Bun secrets
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now stores its bearer token in the operating system credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service) through `Bun.secrets` instead of leaving it in `credentials.json`. A new `auth-token-store.ts` module wraps `Bun.secrets` with a 2 second timeout, and `loadStoredAuthToken` runs at startup in `cli/src/index.tsx` to load the token into memory or migrate an existing file token into the keychain. The credentials file keeps the user profile with a `tokenStore: 'keychain'` marker and no `authToken`; if the keychain is unavailable the token stays in the owner-only file and the user is never logged out. This addresses a leak where the plain-file token was readable by any local program and had been exposed in a public dotfiles repository.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts` exports `bunSecretStore` and `resolveSecretStore` wrapping `Bun.secrets` with a `KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` of 2000; `cli/src/utils/auth.ts` adds `loadStoredAuthToken` and `moveTokenToKeychain`, which are called in `cli/src/index.tsx` before `parseArgs` and from `saveUserCredentials`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the Codebuff CLI's shared `credentials.json` path is affected, though the module doc states this change is Freebuff-only and the SDK reads the file under Node where `Bun.secrets` is unavailable.

eli5.text: The free coding assistant now keeps your login password in your computer's secure vault instead of a file that any program on your machine could read. This update is for people using the free version of the assistant in their terminal. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant works, and you do not need to take any action; if the secure vault is unavailable, the assistant automatically uses the old file method so you never get logged out.
